headline: Accused Salman Shah murder suspect arrested at Dhaka airport
summary: Mohammad Ashraful Haque, known as Don, was detained while attempting to travel to Saudi Arabia for Umrah.
details: Immigration police arrested Mohammad Ashraful Haque, widely known as Don, at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka today.
The arrest follows a murder case filed with Ramna Police Station regarding the death of legendary actor Salman Shah.
Ashraful was detained around 6:00 am as he attempted to leave the country for Saudi Arabia to perform Umrah.
Police had previously issued a requisition to airport authorities to prevent the accused named in the FIR from leaving Bangladesh.
Following the arrest, the suspect was handed over to the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) and produced before a court.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Md Jewel Rana has sent the accused to jail after police sought his confinement.
Salman Shah, born Shahriar Chowdhury Emon, was a cinematic icon of the 1990s who died at the age of 25 on September 6, 1996.
caption:
A suspect in the 1996 murder of actor Salman Shah is arrested at the airport while trying to leave the country.

Immigration police arrested Mohammad Ashraful Haque, widely known as Don, at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka today.

The arrest follows a murder case filed with Ramna Police Station regarding the death of legendary actor Salman Shah.

Ashraful was detained around 6:00 am as he attempted to leave the country for Saudi Arabia to perform Umrah.

Police had previously issued a requisition to airport authorities to prevent the accused named in the FIR from leaving Bangladesh.

Following the arrest, the suspect was handed over to the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) and produced before a court.

Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Md Jewel Rana has sent the accused to jail after police sought his confinement.

Salman Shah, born Shahriar Chowdhury Emon, was a cinematic icon of the 1990s who died at the age of 25 on September 6, 1996.

headline: 873 dead as measles outbreak claims 6 more lives in 24 hours
summary: The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) reports a surge in suspected cases, with the national death toll reaching 873 this year.
details: Six more patients died with measles-like symptoms in 24 hours, bringing the total number of confirmed and suspected measles-related deaths to 873 this year, according to the DGHS.
The latest fatalities were all suspected measles deaths. This brings the total number of suspected deaths to 775, while laboratory-confirmed deaths remain at 98.
In the last 24 hours, 988 new suspected measles cases were reported, raising the cumulative number of suspected cases nationwide to 136,320.
Additionally, 75 new confirmed measles cases were recorded, bringing the total number of laboratory-confirmed infections to 17,115.
Since March 15 this year, 118,382 patients with suspected measles have been hospitalized across the country.
Of those hospitalized, 114,142 patients have recovered, according to data provided by the DGHS.
